args.summary: checkout-api (v2.3.1) began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) after the latest deploy, with an elevated error rate (~18%). Action taken: rolled back all production regions to the most recent healthy release, v2.3.0. Rollback completed and verified. Next steps: investigate the v2.3.1 regression before any re-deployment attempt.
args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened:

1. **Diagnosis**: The latest production deploy, v2.3.1, was unhealthy in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an ~18% error rate.
2. **Rollback**: Rolled checkout-api back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release that was healthy in production, across all regions.
3. **Verification**: Confirmed the service is now healthy with an error rate of 0.2%.
4. **Incident**: Opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** describing the failure and the rollback action; the on-call engineer has been paged.

transcript.content: I'll first check the deployment history and current service status to identify the last healthy release.

transcript.content: The production history shows v2.3.1 is unhealthy, and the most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0. I'll roll back to that version now.

Rollback then incident — incident describes rollback, so do rollback first, then create incident. Actually could be parallel, but incident summary should reflect the rollback action; safer to rollback first.

transcript.content: The rollback completed. Now I'll verify the service is healthy and open the SEV2 incident.
